Develop AI workflows: Build and test LLM, RAG, and tool-using agent workflows for assigned use cases.
Evaluate approaches: Compare LLMs, embedding models, and retrieval methods against quality, reliability, latency, and cost, using evaluation criteria and methods set by senior team members.
Maintain evaluation assets: Create and update representative test cases, benchmark datasets, and regression checks; report results and limitations.
Improve retrieval quality: Develop and tune RAG pipelines, including embeddings, retrieval, reranking, and grounding, based on evaluation results.
Investigate failures: Review incorrect answers, retrieval misses, and workflow failures; implement and measure improvements.
Support production workflows: Use experimentation, tracing, and observability tools to help monitor systems and investigate performance changes.
Collaborate on delivery: Work with engineering, product, and domain partners to clarify requirements, communicate findings, and deliver practical AI solutions.
Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative or technical field.
3+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, applied AI, or a related field.
Hands-on experience developing applications with LLMs and evaluating their outputs.
Strong Python, data analysis, and problem-solving skills.
Understanding of embeddings, semantic search, retrieval, RAG and evaluation metrics.
Experience with an agent framework such as PydanticAI, LangGraph, or a similar tool.
Ability to design useful test cases, interpret evaluation results, and identify limitations.
Familiarity with cloud data or ML platforms, Git, testing, and collaborative software development.
Clear communication with technical and nontechnical colleagues.
Experience with Databricks, evaluation platforms, production deployment, fine-tuning, distributed processing, or healthcare data is beneficial but not required.
This is an individual contributor role with no people-management responsibilities.
Works independently on defined analyses and implementation tasks, with guidance on project priorities and broader technical direction.
Makes day-to-day decisions about experiments, test cases, and implementation details within agreed project goals.
Recommends model and retrieval improvements based on results; escalates major architecture changes, sensitive-data concerns, significant cost implications, and production release decisions to senior team members or the appropriate owners.
Influences assigned projects through implementation and evidence, rather than owning the evaluation strategy or technical direction across multiple projects.
